findings.title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record is missing
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the logged-in user has never interacted with the topic (no row in topic_users). The very next line `if tu.notification_level > ...` then dereferences nil and raises NoMethodError, turning a normal first-time visit into a 500. The code should either create a record via `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` (which already handles the insert path) or bail out cleanly when tu is nil.

findings.title: GET request mutates notification state (CSRF + no confirmation)
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is wired to `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (see config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and silently flips the caller's TopicUser.notification_level as a side effect of loading the page. There is no CSRF token check (Rails protects only non-GET by default), no confirmation step, and no redirect after save — so any cross-site link, image hot-link, or browser prefetch that a logged-in user triggers against a known topic_id will toggle their notification level without consent, and a simple F5 re-toggles it (muted→regular→muted). It should be a POST with a confirm form, or at minimum redirect to the canonical topic URL after writing so refresh is idempotent.

findings.title: Refreshing the unsubscribe page re-applies the toggle
findings.body: After `tu.save!` the action falls through to `perform_show_response`, which renders the `show` template while the browser URL is still `/t/.../unsubscribe`. Reloading the page re-enters `unsubscribe`, re-reads the (now changed) notification_level, and flips it again. There is no `redirect_to` after the write, so the side effect is not idempotent — a user who refreshes once after unsubscribing from a 'watching' topic ends up muted, and a second refresh is a no-op, but the level they see in the UI does not match what they expect.

findings.title: No specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe
findings.body: A new state-changing controller action is added (toggles notification_level, requires login, supports slug/id redirect, falls back to show template) but there are no corresponding request/controller specs covering: happy path toggle, idempotency/refresh, behavior when no TopicUser row exists, behavior for topics the user cannot see, and the redirect when slugs_do_not_match. Only a tiny tweak to message_builder_spec was added.

findings.title: Toggle sends already-regular users to muted with no warning
findings.body: The branch `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ... else ... muted` means a single click of the per-topic unsubscribe link on an account that is already at 'regular' silently demotes them to 'muted'. The I18n copy in client.en.yml ('You will stop receiving notifications...') is shown only on the Ember page; the non-JS GET fallback never shows it and never asks. Combined with the GET/refresh issue above, this is the path users will actually hit from email clients without JavaScript.

findings.title: Typo in computed property name: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (three i's, 'Notificiations'). Templates and any future callers have to match this misspelling; it should be `stopNotificationsText`. There is no second typo'd alias, so renaming is safe.

findings.title: Triple-stash on interpolated I18n string is XSS-prone if title ever flows from user input without escaping
findings.body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` is rendered unescaped because the I18n string embeds `<strong>`. The `title` interpolation currently comes from `model.fancyTitle`, which html_escapes in Topic#fancy_title, so today this is safe — but the pattern is fragile: any future change that lets the title (or the surrounding I18n string) include raw HTML from a less-trusted source will inject script. Prefer rendering the strong tags from the template and using `{{title}}` (double-stash) for the topic title.

findings.title: No error handling if PostStream.loadTopicView rejects
findings.body: The `model` hook returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` with no `.catch`. If the user cannot see the topic (deleted, secured category, PM they're not a participant in), the promise rejects and Ember shows the generic error route, which is jarring for what is supposed to be a friendly unsubscribe confirmation page. Also, `params.id` is the route param but the same value is read from `params.id` here and the controller uses `params[:topic_id]` — fine for routing but worth noting that the slug from the route is never validated against `topic.slug`, unlike the Rails side.

findings.title: Unsubscribe spec passes unsubscribe_url but never asserts on it
findings.body: The new spec passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the builder but only asserts the existence of the `List-Unsubscribe` header and that the body contains `user_preferences_url`. There is no expectation that `unsubscribe_url` actually appears in the rendered body or HTML — which is the entire point of the new translation key in server.en.yml. Without that assertion a regression that drops the interpolation variable would still pass.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url interpolation has no fallback and is silently dropped
findings.body: The new line `To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).` references `%{unsubscribe_url}` but only the notification emails path (`send_notification_email` in user_notifications.rb) sets this key. All other callers of `build_email` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (e.g., signup, forgot_password, admin_login, signup_after_approval, authorize_email, account_created) do not pass `unsubscribe_url`, so I18n will raise MissingInterpolationArgument or leave a literal `%{unsubscribe_url}` in the email body depending on the I18n backend. Either guard the interpolation (`%{unsubscribe_url}` only when present) or make `unsubscribe_url` default to nil in Email::MessageBuilder.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url points at GET endpoint that mutates state
findings.body: `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` is now embedded in every notification email body, but as noted above that URL is a GET handler that immediately toggles the user's notification level (no confirmation). Clicking it from an email preview pane, a link-checker, or any URL sanitizer that fetches links will silently change the user's settings. This should be a confirmation page, not the destructive endpoint.

findings.title: Two competing /unsubscribe routes with no clear precedence doc
findings.body: Routes `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` are both added to map to `topics#unsubscribe`. The non-slug form will match `/t/1234/unsubscribe` before the slugged form because it is listed first. The unsubscribe emails use `Topic#unsubscribe_url` which always includes the slug, so the slugged form is the one that actually fires — but the bare-id form silently swallows anything that looks like `t/<digits>/unsubscribe`, which could mask future routing bugs. Either remove the bare-id form or document why both are required.

findings.title: Duplicate %{respond_instructions} placeholder rendered twice when context posts present
findings.body: The template now contains two `%{respond_instructions}` placeholders — one inside the `if context_posts.present?` branch (line 6) and one after the closing `end` (line 19). `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` calls `html_override.gsub!('%{respond_instructions}', respond_instructions)`, which substitutes both, so it works, but it means the instructions are rendered twice in long emails (once above the previous discussion, once at the bottom). Verify this is intentional; otherwise remove the inner one.
